title: Dependability Factory Launch — 90-Day Cadence Brief
content:
Purpose and high level concept:

This brief outlines the first 90 days of the Dependability Factory: a programmatic intake, stabilization, and handoff pipeline to get product services from ‘no-SLO’ to ‘operational SLO’ with minimal friction. The factory is intended to run as a cross-functional assembly line (intake -> instrumentation -> SLO design -> experiments -> rollout -> handoff) with a repeating 2-week sprint cadence and a lightweight governance council.

Why a factory model?
- Many teams are stuck in ad-hoc SLO projects that stall due to ambiguity (metrics, ownership, dashboards).
- The factory formalizes repeatable steps, clear owners at each stage, and fast feedback loops so the org can scale dependability adoption.
- Focus on minimal viable SLOs (MVSLOs) first: measurable, actionable, and with clear mitigation paths.

Objectives for 90 days (SMART):
1) Launch intake funnel and onboard 10 services into the pipeline; 6 should reach operational SLOs by day 90.
2) Reduce average SLO onboarding lead time from baseline (TBD) to <= 25 days per service.
3) Publish an Observability Scorecard template and have it used by all onboarded services.
4) Create two reusable runbook templates and integrate them into the incident console.

Program roles and responsibilities
- Program Lead: Ava Martinez — overall coordination, cadence, exec reporting.
- SRE Facilitators: Jordan Kim, Priya Desai — run the workshops, assist with instrumentation decisions, help define error budgets.
- Metrics & Observability Owner: Ethan Shaw — dashboards, query templates, alert guardrails.
- Product Liaison & Safety: Marta Rodriguez — product tradeoffs, rollout gating, customer impact mapping.
- Service Owners: named by product teams — execute instrumentation work and adopt runbooks.
- Dependability Council (weekly 30m): rotating set of engineering leads + SRE facilitators for gating and unblockers.

Intake funnel — how services enter the factory
1) Submission form (Confluence form) with: service name, primary owner, current SLIs, production traffic estimate, blast radius, required SLOs (if any).
2) Triage board (kanban): categorize as Green/Amber/Red based on readiness and customer impact.
3) Kickoff pairing session scheduled within 3 business days for Green/Amber; Red gets prioritized emergency support.

Factory stages and checkpoints
- Stage A: Quick Audit (1–3 days)
  - Goal: inventory existing telemetry, alert fatigue, incident history.
  - Checkpoint: audit doc + scorecard filled (observability score >= threshold to proceed).
- Stage B: Instrumentation Sprint (1–3 weeks)
  - Goal: add any missing SLIs (latency, errors, throughput), ensure dimensions (region, route, model) are recorded.
  - Deliverable: dashboard, SLI queries in standard repo, lightweight dashboard link.
- Stage C: SLO Design Workshop (1 week)
  - Goal: draft MVSLO(s) with owner-validated targets, error budget policy, mitigation playbook.
  - Checkpoint: SLO spec file checked into the SLO repo and approved by Dependability Council.
- Stage D: Canary & Bake (2–3 weeks)
  - Goal: run canary traffic, validate signal stability, exercise fallback flows.
  - Deliverable: canary report, regression notes, final SLO readiness checklist.
- Stage E: Operational Handoff (3 days)
  - Goal: finalize runbook, define escalation chain, schedule recurring SLO review.
  - Checkpoint: SLO becomes part of the service’s on-call rotation and dashboard appears in the SRE console.

Sprint cadence and meeting rhythm
- 2-week sprint cadence with the following recurring touchpoints:
  - Monday: intake grooming (30m) — accept/triage new services.
  - Tuesday: small working sessions for instrumentation (ad-hoc pairing).
  - Wednesday: SLO Design Workshop (1hr) for active services.
  - Friday: Demo + blockers review (45m) — show progress and unblock.
  - Weekly Dependability Council (30m) for gating.

Observability Scorecard (key dimensions)
- SLIs implemented (list): latency p50/p95/p99, success/error rate, throughput, queue depth.
- Data retention and cardinality notes.
- Alert-to-incident ratio.
- Dashboard completeness (end-to-end path visibility).
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for last 3 incidents.

SLO spec template (minimal fields)
- service_name, owner, SLI_query, SLO_target, measurement_window, error_budget_policy, rollback_triggers, fallback_model/version_mapping, customer_impact_description.

Runbooks and incident integration
- Two templates: 1) Operational degradation runbook (latency/throughput), 2) Correctness/data-quality runbook (validation, model drift).
- Each runbook includes: quick triage checklist, mitigation steps (with CLI/runbook commands), escalation trees, public/CS communication draft.
- Runbooks are stored in the central ops-playbooks repo and linked to PagerDuty services.

Risk register (top items)
- Insufficient telemetry on legacy services -> mitigant: prioritized instrumentation pairing and temporary synthetic probes.
- Alert noise leading to ignored signals -> mitigant: apply alert hygiene policy and alert-to-incident thresholds before production rollout.
- Dependency cascade (downstream model infra) -> mitigant: clarify upstream SLOs and add circuit-breaker patterns.

Measurement and success indicators
- # services onboarded to factory and # with operational SLOs.
- Mean days from intake to operational SLO.
- Observability Scorecard average across onboarded services.
- Post-rollout incident frequency for onboarded services (target: <= 10% increase during rollout).

Communications and change management
- Weekly status update (email + short Confluence update) highlighting newly onboarded services, blocked items, and SLO adoption stats.
- Monthly exec one-pager for product and leadership summarizing outcomes and risks.
- Office hours (virtual) twice weekly during the launch quarter for hands-on help.

Operational tooling and templates (deliverables by day 30)
- Intake form and triage board.
- Standard SLI query templates for common stacks (k8s, envoy, inference runtime).
- Observability Scorecard doc and automated scoring script (basic).
- Two runbook templates and one SLO spec template.

Handoff and long-term governance
- After operational handoff, Service Owners own the SLO, with quarterly reviews led by SRE facilitators for the first year.
- Dependability Council transitions from gating to a quarterly audit/lessons-learned forum.

Immediate next steps (week 0–2)
1) Publish intake form and open first intake wave (target 10 services).
2) Run onboarding workshop with the first 4 service owners.
3) Deliver the Observability Scorecard template and run the first audits.
4) Create the Dependability Council recurring invite and invite stakeholders.

Open questions for the council
- What minimum observability score should block progression to Stage B? Recommendation: 50/100.
- Which teams must mandatorily participate in the first cohort? Recommendation: Hosting, Serving Runtime, Console.
- Is an executive SLA required for any service in the first cohort?

Appendix: sample SLOs (examples)
- Text-generation API: availability SLO = 99.95% over 30d window (measured as successful request completion within 3s).
- Embeddings batch job: freshness SLO = 95% within 60m for queued jobs.
- Dedicated inference pool: throughput SLO = 90th percentile throughput per minute above baseline for committed capacity.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight; we will iterate the cadence and checkpoints after the first cohort.
- Please comment inline on the intake criteria and risk mitigations.

---
Document owner: Ava Martinez (eng-sre).
